description: Tracks sales pipeline, customer records and business workflows.

sources.note: The edition table lists REST, SOAP, bulk and event surfaces and names editions with and without access.
Quick start signs up for a free Developer Edition and updates a record.
The quick start obtains an OAuth-connected access token and passes it as a bearer credential.
Salesforce publishes a catalog of its hosted MCP servers.

access_note: Free Developer Edition supports development. Production API availability depends on the customer edition.
blocker: Several customer editions lack API access or require an add-on.
toolkit: Start with read-only account and opportunity lookups, then add scoped record updates.
unknowns: Confirm the customer edition before onboarding.

description: Manages customer relationships across sales, marketing and service.

sources.note: Developer onboarding lists REST APIs, OAuth and webhooks.
The developer guide describes free test accounts and a private-app access token for a single portal.
The deals guide describes the deal object and associated CRM records.
HubSpot hosts its own OAuth-protected remote MCP server with CRM reads and writes.

access_note: Free developer test accounts provide isolated data and a time-limited Enterprise trial.
blocker: No initial credential gate identified for a developer test account.
toolkit: Build a deal briefing across company, deal and activity records.
unknowns: Feature entitlement in each customer portal depends on its subscription.

description: Tracks deals, sales activities and customer contacts through a pipeline.

sources.note: Getting started distinguishes OAuth applications from integrations using a personal API token and identifies the API as RESTful.
The authentication example requests the deals resource.
The product page includes API access in every plan, describes CRM sync, and links the trial.
Developer sandbox access is requested through a form.
Pipedrive documents its native MCP server.

access_note: A 14-day trial is available. Every plan includes API-token access. The dedicated developer sandbox has a request form.
blocker: A personal integration can start on a trial. Public distribution uses the app path.
toolkit: Sync deals and their pipeline stage as narrow, separately permissioned tools.
unknowns: Sandbox approval turnaround was not established.

description: Stores customer and company records in a customizable relationship workspace.

sources.note: The platform lists REST, its separate app SDK, read/write operations, webhooks and OAuth 2.0.
The plan guide says the API is available on every plan.
The workspace settings guide explains API-key creation and administrator management.
The meetings endpoint finds or creates a meeting linked to CRM records.
Attio documents a native MCP connection on all plans.

access_note: API access is included on all plans, including Free. Workspace admins manage API keys.
blocker: A free workspace can use the API within its granted scopes.
toolkit: Start with record search and updates. Use webhooks to keep records current.
unknowns: Validate write scopes for each object.

description: Offers a self-hostable CRM with workspace-defined objects and relationships.

sources.note: Twenty generates REST and GraphQL APIs for each workspace. The guide describes keys and CRUD on people, companies, opportunities and custom objects.
The project documents self-hosting with Docker Compose.
The vendor documents workspace MCP endpoints for cloud and self-hosted instances, with OAuth or API-key authentication.

access_note: Run the open-source CRM on infrastructure you control and create a workspace API key. Cloud plan terms were not verified.
blocker: Custom object names and schemas vary by workspace.
toolkit: Inspect the workspace schema before generating object-specific tools.
unknowns: Cloud-hosted subscription restrictions were not verified.

description: Organizes work through customizable apps, items and tasks.

sources.note: FAQ confirms full API access on free accounts, client credentials under account settings and two rate-limit buckets.
The authentication guide specifies OAuth2 including a single-app grant.
The reference lists resources for items, tasks, contacts, files and many other objects.
API conventions document HTTP resource URLs, verbs and JSON representations.
Podio parent Progress documents a server connecting AI assistants directly to Podio data.

access_note: Free and paid accounts can register an API client in settings under the same base rate limits.
blocker: The base rate limits apply per integration.
toolkit: Start with task and item retrieval scoped to one workspace.
unknowns: Check the required scopes before allowing writes.

description: Manages leads, accounts, deals and configurable sales modules.

sources.note: Zoho describes a free Developer Edition, REST APIs and vendor SDKs.
The limits table assigns API credits to Free Edition and describes concurrency limits.
The GraphQL guide defines its authorization requirements.
The versioned reference groups metadata, records and bulk operations.
Zoho CRM publishes its own MCP overview.

access_note: Free Developer Edition is available. Free CRM accounts also receive a daily API-credit allowance.
capabilities: Work with metadata and bulk APIs
blocker: Usage credits vary by edition, and GraphQL has separate permissions.
toolkit: Expose scoped record search first. Check organization credits before bulk jobs.
unknowns: Verify GraphQL entitlement for the target CRM edition.

description: Combines lead and opportunity records with sales communication.

sources.note: Close documents its REST API, native MCP, OAuth2 and API keys, and describes requesting a free partner developer organization.
Internal API keys are transmitted through HTTP Basic.
Pricing lists a 14-day trial and MCP access on each plan.
Developer reference links CRM resources including leads, contacts and opportunities.

access_note: The product has a 14-day trial. Noncustomer integration partners can request a free developer organization by email.
blocker: Persistent complimentary partner access needs a separate request.
toolkit: Provide lead and opportunity lookups with optional contact creation.
unknowns: Free developer-organization approval turnaround is unknown.

description: Manages sales records and customer relationships alongside Google Workspace.

sources.note: Authentication guide distinguishes API keys from OAuth2 for partner integrations.
Copper specifies its trial, Professional and Business plans and a JSON REST interface.
Key guide describes creating, reading, updating and deleting Copper data.
Copper distinguishes its own MCP server from third-party connectors.
OAuth app registration requires emailing Copper partners with the application purpose and callback URL.

access_note: API access is documented for trials and the Professional and Business subscriptions. Third-party OAuth client registration requires contacting Copper.
blocker: Continued use requires an API-enabled production tier.
toolkit: Offer record lookup after checking the customer subscription and preferred OAuth path.
unknowns: Partner OAuth credential issuance time was not established.

description: Manages transactions, deal pipelines and relationships for capital markets teams.

sources.note: API-key instructions require a user group enabled under Admin and refer customers to their admin or CSM.
The key and client ID are exchanged using OAuth2 client credentials for a scoped bearer token.
The portal separates Schema and Data APIs and describes data operations on entries.
The query reference exposes filters against data rows.
DealCloud provides a tenant MCP server with a Celeste license and explicit MCP access capabilities.

access_note: An existing DealCloud site administrator or customer success manager must enable API capability on the user group. The user can then enable a personal key.
blocker: API-enabled user-group membership and a customer site are prerequisites.
toolkit: Build schema-aware entry search once a design partner provisions a tenant and scoped credentials.
unknowns: Public developer trial terms were not established.

description: Provides customer support ticketing, agent workflows and a help center.

sources.note: Trial lasts 14 days. A sponsored development account is available through the partner program.
The Ticketing API quick start uses HTTP resource endpoints to create and inspect tickets.
Existing tokens use Basic authentication with an email. OAuth is available for API requests.
Migration timeline blocks creating new tokens from October 27, 2026. Existing active tokens stop working by April 30, 2027. Third-party integrations must use OAuth.
Zendesk Bridge EAP connects external clients to the Zendesk MCP server for ticket, user and help-center operations.

access_note: Free 14-day development trial. Historical accounts may retain active API tokens until April 2027. New tokens can no longer be created.
blocker: New integrations need OAuth. Customer API tokens cannot be used to authenticate multi-customer apps.
toolkit: Use OAuth for new ticket tools. Keep the early-access vendor MCP optional.
unknowns: Public distribution and EAP participation have separate requirements.

description: Supports customer conversations, contacts and workspaces through an omnichannel inbox.

sources.note: The platform describes free US development workspaces, REST, webhooks, private apps and public-app review.
Authentication guide distinguishes an access token for an installed workspace from OAuth for customer installs.
Intercom hosts a remote MCP server for contacts and conversations, currently for US-hosted workspaces.

access_note: Free US development workspace. A private app can use its workspace token. Access to other customers requires OAuth and public-app review.
blocker: Free development workspaces are region- and feature-limited.
toolkit: Pilot conversation and contact reads in a development workspace.
unknowns: Check whether the customer region supports Intercom’s native MCP.

description: Manages support tickets, agents and customer contacts.

sources.note: Freshdesk sets a trial API rate and lists plan-specific limits for ticket and contact endpoints.
The v2 reference shows agent endpoints and an API key in HTTP Basic authentication.
Freshworks separately documents OAuth apps calling the Freshdesk REST API.
Freshworks provides a Freshdesk MCP server with plan-specific action quotas and API-key authentication.

access_note: During a trial the API permits 50 requests per minute. Post-trial limits and access depend on the helpdesk plan.
blocker: Trial and production quotas differ, and ongoing API access depends on the plan.
toolkit: Start with ticket lookup and contact retrieval within the account rate limit.
unknowns: Confirm entitlement and quotas against the tenant’s current plan.

description: Routes customer conversations across shared inboxes and channels.

sources.note: Front links a free development-account signup and describes its partner publishing process.
Company-scoped API tokens authenticate scripts, while OAuth is required for partner updates absent an exception.
Core API tutorial creates and updates contacts and sends attachments through HTTP resource requests.
Front operates an OAuth-authenticated MCP endpoint for conversation data.

access_note: Front offers a free development account. Company API tokens work for internal scripts. Partners normally need OAuth.
blocker: Partners acting on customer accounts must implement OAuth absent a vendor exception.
toolkit: Prototype contact and conversation tools in a developer account and use OAuth for customer installs.
unknowns: Confirm the customer plan for any advanced scopes.

description: Tracks B2B support issues, accounts and contacts across customer channels.

sources.note: A dashboard token is passed in the Bearer authorization header.
Token creation requires the manage-API-tokens permission or admin intervention.
The reference separates issue, account, contact, message and knowledge-base endpoints.
Pylon documents interactive OAuth for its own MCP, with token-based headless access through its REST API.

access_note: An existing workspace user needs permission to manage API tokens. Other users must request the capability from an admin.
blocker: A permitted workspace role must provision the REST token. MCP requires interactive OAuth.
toolkit: Use the API for background issue sync and the native MCP for user-authorized interactive work.
unknowns: No standalone free API sandbox was confirmed.

description: Combines email, chat and calls in a customer service helpdesk.

sources.note: LiveAgent offers a 30-day no-card trial with all features.
An administrator creates v3 API keys in Configuration and chooses their permissions.
The HTTP v3 reference lists agents, tickets, chats, contacts, files and calls.
Built-in MCP endpoint allows external agents to act with the user identity, including OAuth 2.1.

access_note: A 30-day no-card trial includes the features. An administrator can issue scoped v3 keys.
blocker: An administrator creates a scoped key for an existing tenant.
toolkit: Start with ticket search using a scoped API key. Offer the built-in MCP for per-agent access.
unknowns: Confirm endpoint version for each tool because v3 and v4 coexist.

description: Manages B2B customer support threads, accounts and customer timelines.

sources.note: Plain’s plan guide says every plan starts with a seven-day trial without a card.
Plain describes GraphQL and scoped machine-user API keys for customer, thread and label operations.
Migration guide documents account GraphQL operations and the vendor SDK.
Plain’s release announcement documents a native MCP server for threads, customers and user-permitted actions.
Pipedream separately offers a Plain MCP connector through its managed endpoint.

access_note: Seven-day no-card trials are offered. Machine users receive keys scoped to specific operations.
blocker: Machine-user permissions determine which queries and mutations will succeed.
toolkit: Use a scoped machine user to read support threads and create labelled follow-up work.
unknowns: Confirm the workspace subscription for ongoing production use.

description: Provides shared support inboxes and a customer-facing knowledge base.

sources.note: Vendor plan table excludes the Free plan and reporting on Standard.
The JSON-over-HTTPS Inbox API includes a PHP SDK and linked resources.
Inbox API supports OAuth2 authorization code and client credentials. Each credential must belong to an active invited user.
Help Scout provides an official MCP server on API-enabled plans and documents the separate API key used for Docs.

access_note: The Free plan explicitly excludes APIs. Standard allows core operations. Reporting endpoints require Plus or Pro.
blocker: The plan determines access to the API and reports. OAuth credentials must belong to an active invited user.
toolkit: Offer conversation lookup on Standard and conditionally expose reporting on higher tiers.
unknowns: Trial API entitlement was not confirmed.

description: Brings ecommerce customer conversations, tickets and order context into a helpdesk.

sources.note: All helpdesk plans support REST. Owner/admin keys use email and key through HTTP Basic.
OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps, while API keys are for private apps.
Guide starts with a trial and requires a draft app and email request to obtain the developer sandbox.
The developer portal workflow includes submitting the public app for review.
Gorgias documents the support tools available through its MCP server.

access_note: Trial accounts are the entry point. Owners and admins can create keys. Persistent developer sandboxes require a draft app and approval.
blocker: Public distribution requires OAuth and app review. Converting the trial to a developer sandbox requires vendor approval.
toolkit: Validate ticket reads in a trial before requesting the persistent partner sandbox.
unknowns: Public app approval time was not established.

description: Organizes customer conversations and tasks around a shared customer profile.

sources.note: The REST reference includes customer tasks and conversation events and specifies token-based Basic authentication.
Tokens are created by users with the API User role.
The MCP connections feature lets Gladly AI call external servers. Its direction does not establish an outbound Gladly server.

access_note: A Gladly user needs the API User permission before creating the token. A technical admin is the documented implementation starting point.
blocker: A customer tenant and a user with the API User permission are prerequisites.
toolkit: Provide customer timelines and task lookups only after the workspace grants API access.
unknowns: Gladly documents consuming external MCP tools. A vendor server exposing Gladly data was not established.
A free independent developer sandbox was not confirmed.

description: Runs team conversations across channels, messages and shared files.

sources.note: OAuth installation exchanges consent for scoped tokens.
Token reference distinguishes bot and user access tokens.
Basic sandbox entitlement is available to Developer Program members without additional cost.
Web API quotas apply per workspace and method; history and replies have special commercial-distribution limits.
Slack publishes its own MCP tools for search, messaging and files mapped to Web API limits.

access_note: Slack Developer Program members can provision a basic sandbox at no additional cost. Some enhanced sandbox features require a paid plan or payment method.
blocker: Commercial distribution can bring tighter limits on conversation history and replies.
toolkit: Scope tools per workspace and cache conversation lookups; evaluate Marketplace approval for frequent history retrieval.
unknowns: Workspace installation restrictions and rate limits depend on the app and method.

description: Provides programmable messaging, voice and communications infrastructure.

sources.note: The trial guide includes limited product units and sending first messages and calls.
HTTP Basic supports the API key or the Account SID and auth token on applicable resources; SDKs call the REST APIs.
Twilio Support identifies the Twilio Labs project as an unsupported alpha, distinct from a supported official service.
The vendor Labs repository exposes OpenAPI-generated Twilio tools and identifies its experimental status.

access_note: Free trial includes product-specific units with limits; production usage beyond the allowance requires an upgrade.
blocker: Trials restrict quantities and destinations. Live traffic incurs usage charges.
toolkit: Use a read-only communications toolkit or trial-limited messaging prototype with explicit recipient authorization.
unknowns: Twilio Labs publishes an experimental MCP. Support explicitly disclaims an officially supported implementation.

description: Offers organizational chat, channels, meetings and collaboration bots.

sources.note: The REST reference documents OAuth2, users, chats and message resources.
Registration issues OAuth application credentials for Cliq requests.
Developer platform comparison marks API support Yes on all four editions, including Free.
Zoho publishes a guide to its native Cliq MCP server.

access_note: The plan comparison lists API support for Free and all paid tiers. Developers register an OAuth application in the console.
blocker: Endpoint- and organization-specific limits can restrict throughput.
toolkit: Start with channel and message tools using the narrowest OAuth scopes.
unknowns: Confirm the target organization’s installation policy.

description: Combines messaging, shared documents, calendars and collaboration apps.

sources.note: Lark distinguishes scopes usable by a developer before review from permissions requiring approval and additional data-access configuration.
Developer guide explains test companies and users.
User access token refresh uses the OAuth token flow.
Official OpenAPI MCP supports user and tenant tokens and describes message, group, calendar and Base operations.
Server endpoint reference documents reading document content.

access_note: Developers can create test organizations. Some scopes work for the developer without review; tenant-wide production access requires permission approval.
capabilities: Work with calendars and Base records
blocker: Scope approval and data-access ranges depend on app identity and requested resources.
toolkit: Start with a test tenant and release tools one scope at a time for admin approval.
unknowns: Developer test-tenant pricing was not explicitly documented.

description: Provides team messaging, reactions and channels in a shared workspace.

sources.note: The public API add-on is available on every plan. Its guide lists key generation and actions for messages and reactions.
Pricing confirms a free workspace option alongside paid tiers.
Pumble documents its own MCP server and client setup.

access_note: The API add-on is offered on all plans including Free. Install it in the workspace before generating a key.
blocker: The add-on bot must belong to the private channel it needs to read.
toolkit: Build channel and message tools with membership checks for private channels.
unknowns: Confirm workspace-specific permission to install the add-on.

description: Hosts communities with messages, channels, voice and bot interactions.

sources.note: Discord’s reference distinguishes Bot tokens, OAuth2 bearer and Basic for OAuth token endpoints only.
The quick start registers an app, copies a bot token, installs it and configures intents and commands.
Beyond the HTTP API, Discord documents WebSocket Gateway events.
Discord’s bot overview describes bot interactions with servers and users.

access_note: The developer portal issues a bot token for a registered app and allows installation in a test server. No explicit fee schedule was established here.
blocker: User installation, server permissions and enabled Gateway intents govern available actions.
toolkit: Use the documented bot identity for command-driven tools. Keep privileged intents optional.
unknowns: The direct resource credential is a Bot token (Other). Basic applies only to OAuth token endpoints.
An official Discord MCP server for acting on server data was not confirmed.

description: Offers a messaging platform on which developers can run interactive bots.

sources.note: The Bot API is an HTTPS method interface with a per-bot token embedded in the URL. It documents messages, media and updates.
Telegram declares its Bot Platform free to developers and users and explains bot registration.
Bot features document creation through BotFather and available chat behaviours.
Independent telemcp project supports Telegram bot or account access through MCP.

access_note: The Bot Platform is free for developers. Register a bot with BotFather to obtain its per-bot token.
blocker: The bot’s membership and chat permissions constrain what it can observe.
toolkit: Wrap the Bot API for message delivery and update handling with per-chat authorization.
unknowns: The Bot API token is a path credential, not a Bearer header.
An official Telegram MCP was not confirmed.

description: Connects business messaging systems to customers on WhatsApp.

sources.note: Meta’s quick start registers an app, uses a temporary token and test number, sets up a webhook and obtains a system-user token.
Meta’s official Postman collection lists the business portfolio, WABA, phone number and access-token requirements.
Meta’s Graph reference covers business phone numbers.
Meta’s own agentic tools repo names WhatsApp Business Tools MCP and distinguishes setup workflows from other Meta developer tools.
WhatsApp’s pricing page explains production billing by message category.

access_note: Self-registration provides a test phone number and temporary token. Production requires a business portfolio, WhatsApp Business Account and phone number; charges depend on message category.
blocker: Real business assets and messaging permissions are needed for a production sender.
toolkit: Prove routing with test resources, then onboard the customer’s business assets and production token.
unknowns: A no-payment test entitlement was not independently confirmed in the primary sources cited here.

description: Offers a business phone system with call data and conversation intelligence.

sources.note: Aircall separates Basic auth for private tools from OAuth for multi-customer REST integrations.
Vendor reviews public integration requests before issuing the developer account and OAuth credentials; recommends webhooks.
The key guide describes call data, user provisioning and contact management.
Aircall separately provides a seven-day trial of the product.
Aircall describes a beta MCP server with read-only call and conversation intelligence tools.

access_note: Private integrations use Aircall dashboard credentials. Public apps need an approved request for a developer account and OAuth credentials. Aircall also offers a separate product trial.
blocker: Public multi-customer OAuth requires Aircall approval and a customer admin installation.
toolkit: Prototype private call lookups with a customer. Request OAuth credentials before planning a public integration.
unknowns: Trial product availability does not confirm partner OAuth eligibility.

description: Provides APIs for SMS, voice calls and multichannel messaging.

sources.note: The getting-started guide issues key/secret credentials and distinguishes Voice and Messages application setup.
The authentication matrix distinguishes key/secret, Basic and signed JWT bearer credentials by product.
Vonage restricts trial SMS to registered/verified numbers and voice to the registered number.
Vonage’s locally hosted tooling MCP performs SMS, voice and WhatsApp operations, distinct from its docs MCP.

access_note: New users receive API credentials. Free-trial outbound destinations are restricted to registered or verified numbers.
blocker: Full recipient reach needs a paid account. Authentication also varies by API family.
toolkit: Separate Voice and Messages tools by credential type; test against verified numbers.
unknowns: Confirm country-specific sender registration for the intended production route.
